account:
It is day 1, 06:00. Today I should read my appointment books and attend office at 08:00, inspect grain at the mill at 10:00, and attend the great hall lighting inspection at 18:00. My usual schedule also includes lunch at home, council letters at 13:00, tea with the neighbour at 15:00, and afternoon office hours.

Something unusual appears to be being arranged privately. The builder and innkeeper have arranged an inspection of eight lanterns installed in the great hall, including checking light around the tables. The innkeeper repeatedly sought confirmation that I would attend at 18:00. The secretary found bread in one of the hall's four table chests, though no town accounts. Last night the secretary reported that the innkeeper collected bread from the baker and said the inn owes forty-four emeralds, payable after the jubilee. The secretary also said freight wanted their arrangements kept private until today at 18:00. I have not heard these bread-order details directly from the innkeeper, and the original buyer and precise purpose remain unestablished.

My tentative impression is that the bread, lighting and private arrangements may concern a jubilee gathering, perhaps with the lighting inspection serving as the occasion to bring me to the hall. The matching time is suggestive, not proof. I do not know whether there is a surprise or whether all these matters are connected. The innkeeper says the bread is a private expense, so I should not assume misuse of town money.

Separately, the town accounts remain unlocated. The secretary checked the hall tables and asked the builder, baker and innkeeper without finding a ledger or anyone who knew its location. We agreed to review office storage and correspondence this morning. There are also unverified rumours of bakery lights and a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' traced by the neighbour to Townsfolk 02. The neighbour saw no change herself, and I have no evidence of an actual riverfront project.
